population.note: FICTIONAL. Of about 276M adults, 36.0% are current users (≈99.4M) and 48.5% have ever used (≈133.9M). Ever-use rose 8.5 points, inside the 10.5-point limit. That leaves 12.5 points (≈34.5M) who used and are off now, and ≈142M who have never used. Cycling line: about 18.0 points of current users are on a second or later course, and about 5.0 points of the off-now group restarted and stopped again, so (18.0 + 5.0)/48.5 ≈ 47.4% have cycled. That fits ~35% one-year persistence and 36–47% restart within a year. Age check: 18–29: 20% × 52M = 10.4M; 30–49: 39% × 92M = 35.9M; 50–64: 50% × 62M = 31.0M; 65+: 31.5% × 70M = 22.05M; total ≈ 99.35M ≈ 36.0%. Income thirds (≈92M adults each): bottom 34% = 31.3M, middle 36% = 33.1M, top 38% = 35.0M; the average is 36.0. The bottom third rose most (+9.5 points), driven by the Community Metabolic Health Program (≈4.5M users), seven new continuation-standard Medicaid states, and the copay cut. About 2.1M former import users moved onto public product. The top third grew more slowly (+6) and shifted toward the tirzepatide/bimagrumab co-pack. 65+ use rose 21→31.5% as the $25 copay ($0 for LIS) pulled in people who had been waiting, though about one in five older ever-users is still on a bone pause or a post-NAION stop. The off-now 34.5M include ≈6M older adults on medically advised bone pauses, ≈9M who stopped for GI reasons or by choice, and ≈11M cut off by gating, tenure separation or program waitlists. Never-users skew under-30, rural residents of the 13 holdout states, people with contraindications, and refusers by conviction. Pediatric use is 1.5% of ≈73M ≈ 1.1M: ≈0.95M adolescents 12–17 and ≈0.15M children aged 6–11 after the Nov 2035 approval, mostly through Medicaid EPSDT. About one child in two now lives with a parent who is on the drug or cycling off it.

access.public_coverage: FICTIONAL. The Metabolic Health Access Act (Jul 2035) set a single public rate of $179/month for Medicare Part D and Medicaid from Jan 2036, down from $199. The Part D obesity copay fell from $50 to $25, and to $0 for Low-Income Subsidy enrollees. Eligibility (BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with one comorbidity) and the counselling visit are unchanged. Medicare pays 21.5% of fills, ≈21.4M users (≈7.0M for diabetes, ≈14.4M for obesity). All Medicare incretin fills: 21.4M × $179 × 12 ≈ $46.0B gross. Obesity benefit: 14.4M × $179 × 12 ≈ $30.9B gross. Copays: about 70% of obesity users are non-LIS, so 14.4M × 0.7 × $25 × 12 ≈ $3.0B, leaving ≈$27.9B net to the program. Medicaid: the 90% match is now permanent, and 37 states plus DC use the continuation standard, up from 31 plus DC. Medicaid pays 14.1% of fills: ≈14.0M × $179 × 12 ≈ $30.1B gross, of which the federal share at 90% is ≈$27.1B. The new HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program gives the drug free through FQHCs to uninsured or 'incretin-underinsured' adults up to 250% FPL. It covers 4.5% of fills: ≈4.5M × $149 manufacturer program price × 12 ≈ $8.05B, against an $8.5B annual appropriation, with ≈600k on waitlists. Public payers together cover ≈39.9M users (40.1%), more than commercial plans (30.2%). Public money is now the default payer.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India: 100+ semaglutide brands at $5–30/month, including generic oral semaglutide; the Telangana first-filer plant remains under US import alert. China: generic semaglutide, tirzepatide copies, 'research' retatrutide, and now 'myostatin-pathway' peptide kits sold as bimagrumab substitutes. Canada: generic semaglutide at CAD 45–75/month. Brazil, Mexico, Turkey and Egypt also have generics. US: the mid-2035 contingent entry date passed with no launch. The rival filers' settlements are triggered by the first filer launching or forfeiting, and the first filer has sued in D.D.C. to block FDA's 2035 forfeiture determination. That case is pending, so entry is parked until at least 2037.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Managed decline. Alongside the Act, a renewed HHS–manufacturer portal agreement cut direct maintenance prices: injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide fell to $199–249 (from $249–329); the Wegovy pill 50 mg is $229; retatrutide is $349 direct and $1,349 list; MariTide is $449; amycretin $429. The tirzepatide/bimagrumab co-pack launched in Apr 2036 at $799 direct and $1,890 list. Oral starter doses stay at $149–150. In return, manufacturers got three-year price stability and a Section 232 exemption for US-filled product. PBM net is ≈$175–195. Payer mix of ≈99.4M users: commercial 30.2% (30.0M); Medicare 21.5% (21.4M); Medicaid 14.1% (14.0M); HRSA program 4.5% (4.5M); cash/direct 19.7% (19.6M, including ≈3.8M 'calm' and 'focus' subscribers, down from 4.6M); gray 10.0% (9.9M). Sum = 99.4M = 100%. The gray market changed composition. Imported and counterfeit pens and pills fell from ≈7.1M to ≈5.0M users as poor users moved to public product, while compounded and telehealth 'personalised peptide' users grew from near zero to ≈4.9M. They are mostly middle-income people buying retatrutide, cagrilintide blends and fake 'bima' muscle add-ons that no public plan or gated employer plan supplies. Employer coverage fell from 64% to 58%. Small low-wage employers dropped the benefit, which made their staff 'underinsured' and therefore eligible for the HRSA program. About 85% of the employers who still cover use gated designs, and about a third of those add tenure gates. Oral share is ≈40% of users.

mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'calm' and 'focus' subscriptions (low-dose oral semaglutide or Foundayo, ≈3.8M subscribers), now shrinking after the REWARD trial
smoking and vaping cessation (SHAPS trial still enrolling)
'metabolic health' / longevity regimens in concierge practices, now often built on the bimagrumab co-pack
pediatric under-6 use under specialist care (rare)
compounded and 'research' retatrutide and cagrilintide blends through telehealth platforms

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Muscle-preserving combo driver: Lilly filed tirzepatide plus subcutaneous bimagrumab in Feb 2035 on a 72-week phase 3 trial. FDA approved it in Mar 2036, 13 months after filing, with commercial launch in Apr 2036. Results: 22.1% mean weight loss, with lean mass ≈11% of total loss on DEXA versus ≈33% on tirzepatide alone. Muscle spasms, diarrhoea and acne were more frequent. Fewer than 8% of trial participants were over 70, and there are no fracture endpoints, so the label requires a fracture-outcomes postmarketing study. Pediatric driver: Novo's semaglutide sNDA for ages 6–11, filed Oct 2034 on a 68-week trial (≈-18% BMI change versus placebo), was approved Nov 2035 with growth-velocity and DEXA postmarketing requirements. Survodutide's MASH sNDA, under review at the start, was approved Oct 2035. Lilly's next-generation orals remain in development and unfiled, so they are not on the market. The SHAPS smoking trial is still enrolling. No US generics. Incretin market ≈$221B in 2036. US ≈$199B: ≈89.5M paying users (99.4M − 9.9M gray) × ≈$185 average net × 12 ≈ $198.7B. Ex-US ≈$22B and still eroding.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the most common effect and the leading cause of voluntary stops. Diarrhoea is more frequent with the bimagrumab co-pack. Children 6–11 show vomiting rates similar to adolescents.
Rising in absolute numbers with the larger 65+ user base.
No causal confirmation; absolute risk low. Compounded and counterfeit product still confounds reporting.

Now treated as a national population problem. ≈2.4M long-term Medicare users meet sarcopenia criteria in claims, up from 1.6M. Lean mass is ~30–40% of loss in untrained users over 50. The bimagrumab co-pack cuts this to ≈11% in trial, but almost no Medicare users can get it.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class label. The Apr 2035 HHS 'Strong Aging' priority designation followed the Trustees' fracture score. The Act funds $600M in DEXA and supervised-strength grants. CMS added a baseline-and-12-month DEXA requirement for all new Medicare obesity-benefit users. A CMS national coverage analysis of the co-pack opened in May 2036.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈10.5M users aged 65+ have more than 2 years' use. 10.5M × ~0.6%/yr baseline hip-fracture rate × 0.35 excess ≈ 22,000 excess hip fractures a year. The 2035 Medicare Trustees report scored this for the first time: ≈22,000 × ≈$45k acute and post-acute cost ≈ $1.0B a year to Part A and Medicare Advantage. The vertebral-fracture tail among cycling postmenopausal women 50–64 continues. DEXA waits are 8–12 weeks.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Bone endpoints required in all filings; CMS 90-day bone-pause code retained; private gated plans still not bound by it. The DOJ civil case against Novo was settled in 2035 for an undisclosed sum without admission. The co-pack label makes no bone claim.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Relative risk ≈1.7. ≈99.4M users × ~4/100,000 baseline × 0.7 ≈ 2,800 excess cases a year, mostly partial, permanent vision loss in one eye.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warnings and Precautions statement on all GLP-1 receptor agonist products, unchanged and not boxed. MDL consolidated in 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No causal association; the REWARD trial also found none.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia, 'the grey')
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The NIH-funded REWARD randomised trial (n≈3,200, 52 weeks) read out in Nov 2035. At 12 mg retatrutide, clinically meaningful anhedonia was 9.1% versus 4.0% on placebo, dose-dependent. At low-dose oral semaglutide the difference (3.1% vs 2.6%) was not significant. The same trial found no anxiety benefit at 'calm' doses beyond placebo.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Jan 2036: added to Adverse Reactions ('uncommon: anhedonia, decreased interest in pleasurable activities') for retatrutide and tirzepatide ≥10 mg, plus a Medication Guide line class-wide. Not a Warning. FTC consent orders stand.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Forced stops from tenure separation and HRSA waitlists replace shortage stops. Children who stop are an emerging cohort.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CMS bone-pause code softens it for Medicare; pediatric discontinuation guidance pending.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Iron, B12, vitamin D, calcium and protein insufficiency in high-loss older users and in gray users with no clinical contact; now screened in children 6–11.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Part D and HRSA counselling templates screen for it; AAP guidance; no FDA action.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~10 years; adolescent exposure; repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About fourteen years of follow-up. The 2035 adolescent bone readout showed modestly lower bone-accrual z-scores (≈-0.2) at 2 years, of uncertain lasting significance. Cycling still looks worse for bone than continuous use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Postmarketing requirements continue; adolescent labels updated with bone-accrual language in 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: The gray market regrew and changed shape. Imports fell to ≈5.0M users, while compounded and telehealth peptide users rose to ≈4.9M. Poison-centre GLP-1 calls are roughly flat on 2034, with dosing errors now concentrated in compounded retatrutide 'titration kits'. There has been no contamination cluster on the 2033 scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA warning letters to 41 telehealth platforms (Jun 2036). FDA says Florida's 2035 compounding statute is preempted, and that litigation is pending. Import alerts continue. Still no individual prosecutions.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Seized lots still test at 0–300% of labelled content. Volume has fallen in states with HRSA FQHC uptake.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA public warnings; NABP verified-pharmacy guidance; no new law.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg; usually transient.

safety_ledger.effect: Falls and frailty-related injury in older users
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Fall-related ED visits remain elevated in 65+ users with more than 2 years' use, rising in absolute terms with the 65+ band. Monocular vision loss after NAION is a cited cofactor in a minority of cases.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Fall-risk screening mandatory in the Part D counselling visit; Strong Aging grants fund supervised strength programmes.

safety_ledger.effect: Adverse body-composition cycling (fat-dominant regain after lean-dominant loss)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Upgraded from emerging after pooled DEXA cohorts (2035) confirmed more visceral fat and less lean mass at the same weight after two or more cycles. Concentrated in over-50s cut off by gating, tenure separation or waitlists.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Endocrine and geriatric societies issued joint guidance in 2035 favouring continuous low-dose maintenance plus resistance training over repeated stops. No regulatory action.

safety_ledger.effect: Heart-rate elevation at high triple-agonist doses
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Mean resting heart-rate rise of several bpm at 12 mg retatrutide; CV outcomes trial still ongoing.

Muscle spasms (~20%), diarrhoea, acne, and small haemoglobin shifts in trial. Effects over 72 weeks, in over-70s and on fractures are unknown. Gray 'myostatin peptide' kits sold as substitutes contain unverified actives or none.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; fracture-outcome and long-term safety PMRs; FDA consumer warning on 'bima' peptide kits.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: ≈150k children exposed in the first year. Growth velocity and pubertal timing are being monitored, and nutritional adequacy is the main clinical worry.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Growth-velocity and DEXA PMRs; label requires paediatric-specialist initiation; Medicaid EPSDT covers it.

food_and_beverage.state: With 36% of adults on the drug, salty-snack volume keeps falling ~4% a year and confectionery ~5%. Two PE candy roll-ups sold brands to Mexican and Indian buyers. Protein and 'bone-forward' dairy lead. After the pediatric approval, school-food vendors and kids' brands launched 'growth-first' small-portion, high-protein lines aimed at medicated children. Discount grocers in Dayton and Maryvale now sell both FQHC-recommended protein staples and calorie-dense value packs for people who are off.

alcohol.state: Ninth straight year of spirits volume decline. Beer is down, and NA and single-serve formats hold. Tobacco and vape keep falling faster than the pre-2028 trend.

restaurants.state: Traffic roughly flat. Spend per cover is down ~12% from 2028 in high-uptake suburbs. Gram-priced protein bowls are standard, kids' menus are being re-portioned, and value buffets in holdout rural states keep their off-drug regulars.

apparel.state: Class sizing has hardened. Premium brands added 'Forte' cuts for the fuller-shouldered co-pack body. The national chain's 'structured' and 'cycle' split spread to two competitors. Children's wear added slim-fit 'growth' ranges. Resale sized for cycling keeps growing.

fitness.state: Still growing, with a split. Strong Aging grants and Medicare Advantage 'prescribed lifting' expanded supervised programmes for older users. Premium gyms lost some 'regimen management' members to the co-pack, which is marketed as muscle without the gym, and are repositioning toward 'Forte-plus-training'. Qualified staff for older lifters remain the constraint.

insurance.state: Public payers are now the default for incretins. Employer coverage fell to 58% as small employers dropped the benefit and pointed staff to the HRSA program. Large employers keep gated and tenure-gated designs and do not cover the co-pack. Pharmacy trend is ~+6%, with volume up and price down. The first Trustees fracture score put ≈$1.0B a year on Part A. Life insurers still price untreated BMI ≥30.

pharma.state: Volume is up ~27% (78M → 99.4M users) and average net price is down ~7%. Lilly leads on tirzepatide, retatrutide, Foundayo and the bimagrumab co-pack. Novo holds orals and pediatrics. Amgen grows MariTide. Ex-US revenue erodes to Indian and Chinese generics. Medicare and Medicaid at $179 now account for more volume than commercial plans, so margin comes from commercial plans and the co-pack.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Income, and now the specific product you can afford. Full shoulders and DEXA-verified lean mass on a thin frame (the 'Forte body') read as top-third cash or concierge buying of the $799 co-pack. A lean, soft 'program body' reads as Medicaid, HRSA or Medicare on the 50 mg pill. Gym-hard men with skin flare and a racing pulse read as compounded retatrutide from a telehealth site. Visible cycling and the thin-armed stoop in over-65s read as waitlists, tenure separation or a bone pause.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Use rates now nearly converge (34% bottom, 38% top) because public money pays, but muscle has become the paid upgrade. In Phoenix, Scottsdale women 50–64 on the co-pack and Maryvale women 50–64 on HRSA pills have similar weights and opposite DEXA reports. Houston's medical-centre staff are a visible mix of both. Women 50–64 remain the most sharply sorted group.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Protein-first meals are the default. Parents of medicated 6–11-year-olds plan 'growth plates' at birthday parties. Sunday full-table dinners and church potlucks in Memphis and Houston persist as heritage, and increasingly as where off and cycling families eat.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps keep the on/off/pausing field. 'Forte' in a profile reads as money the way 'coached' did. 'Program' is neutral. 'Unmedicated' remains a niche identity. Advice columns now field partners' worries about telehealth peptide kits rather than parcel pens.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Medicalised and publicly financed. A coalition of paediatricians, eating-disorder clinicians and religious conservatives now fights the under-12 approval. A smaller strand calls the co-pack 'buying your muscle back'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. REWARD found a 5.1-point excess (9.1% vs 4.0%) at 12 mg retatrutide and no significant excess at low-dose oral semaglutide. About 5M Americans are on retatrutide 12 mg, so if the trial rate holds, that is ≈255k excess cases (5M × 0.051). Tirzepatide ≥10 mg carries the label line on extrapolation. The ≈3.8M low-dose 'calm' subscribers are now measured and largely cleared of blunting, and also largely cleared of benefit. Compounded retatrutide users (≈2M within the gray total) dose without measurement.
interior_life.framing: A side effect, in clinic and on the label. 'The grey' has become a clinical shorthand and a line in the Medication Guide. 'Quiet' and 'Even' dropped 'calm' from their homepages after REWARD and now sell 'craving freedom'. Subscriptions fell from 4.6M to 3.8M.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Several large employers removed 'focus' subscriptions from lifestyle accounts in 2036, citing REWARD. Tenure-gated coverage still works as job lock in warehouses and call centres, though less so where the HRSA program catches low-wage workers whose employers dropped the benefit. Unions bargain over whether co-pack coverage is in scope. Fleets keep visual-field checks.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: The 'grey era' label has faded into a period term. Comedy now mocks Forte shoulders and FQHC pill lines rather than flatness. High-stimulus leisure holds. Documentaries have moved on from parcel pens to the telehealth peptide trade.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists use a two-item reward screen for high-dose users, and switching down from 12 mg is a routine suggestion. Couples counselling deals with one partner on Forte and one on the program pill, which is an income gap carried in bodies.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Politics turned from price to who pays and what they get. The Act passed with both parties claiming it, and Safe Pens was stripped in conference. Live fights: CBO's crowd-out estimate of employers dumping workers onto HRSA, Medicare coverage of the co-pack, Florida's compounding statute, and the under-12 approval, which is a campaign issue in 2036 state races.

state.regulatory_posture: FDA is data-demanding. It approved the co-pack with fracture PMRs, approved pediatric 6–11 with growth PMRs, approved the survodutide MASH indication, added the anhedonia adverse-reaction line after an NIH randomised trial, issued 41 telehealth warning letters, and is contesting Florida's compounding statute. It still brings no individual prosecutions, and there is no importation or authentication law.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: The Metabolic Health Access Act (Jul 2035) set a $179 public rate for Medicare and Medicaid from 2036; cut the Part D obesity copay to $25 ($0 LIS); made the 90% Medicaid match permanent, with 100% for the first two years in newly joining states (six states plus one more in 2036 brought the total to 37 plus DC); created the $8.5B/yr HRSA Community Metabolic Health Program giving the drug free through FQHCs; and funded $600M in Strong Aging DEXA and strength grants. There is no individual mandate.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: The CMS continuation standard now applies to the HRSA program too: ≥80% PDC, verified six-monthly weights, 5% response or clinician override, two misses suspend for 6 months, and the 90-day bone-pause code. New Medicare obesity users need DEXA at baseline and at 12 months. Indiana and Arkansas keep their 12-month rules. Kiosk and connected-scale weights now feed a federal program, 37 Medicaid programmes, and private premium tiers. Pediatric growth-chart data flow into EPSDT records.
state.workforce_or_military: DOT sleep-apnea screening still pushes drivers toward tirzepatide, and large fleets run voluntary visual-field checks. The Army adopted Air Force-style accession waivers in 2035 for recruits on stable maintenance for 12 months or more, conditional on DEXA.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: The portal deal exempted US-filled product from Section 232 tariffs, and both firms announced US fill-finish expansion. Chinese API and Indian finished product still supply the import stream and much of the compounding stream. The Telangana import alert and the first filer's forfeiture suit remain a US–India irritant.

events.event: The Medicare Trustees report scores incretin-associated fractures for the first time, putting about 22,000 excess hip fractures and roughly $1.0B a year on Part A. HHS designates sarcopenia and bone loss in long-term users a 'Strong Aging' national priority, and CMS adds DEXA scans at baseline and 12 months for new obesity-benefit users

The President signs the bipartisan Metabolic Health Access Act. It sets a $179 public rate, cuts the Part D copay to $25 ($0 for low-income enrollees), makes the 90% Medicaid match permanent, and funds an $8.5B-a-year HRSA program giving incretins free at community health centres. In the same month Novo and Lilly cut portal maintenance prices to $199–249 under a renewed HHS agreement. The Safe Pens provisions are stripped in conference
events.driver: coverage_shift: public_expansion; state_action: subsidy; price_path: managed_decline

events.event: FDA approves weekly semaglutide for children aged 6 to 11 with obesity on a 68-week trial, requiring specialist initiation and growth and bone monitoring. Medicaid EPSDT coverage follows automatically, and the American Academy of Pediatrics issues cautious guidance

After the NIH-funded REWARD trial finds anhedonia in 9.1% of 12 mg retatrutide users against 4.0% on placebo, and no anxiety benefit at 'calm' doses, FDA adds 'uncommon: anhedonia' to the adverse-reaction sections of high-dose labels. Subscription brands drop 'calm' from their marketing

FDA approves Lilly's tirzepatide-plus-bimagrumab co-pack (filed Feb 2035), which keeps lean mass loss to about 11% of weight lost. It launches at $799 a month direct and is excluded from Medicare's $179 rate pending a coverage review. Ads promise 'strong, not just thin', and a premium chain's 'Forte' cut sells out in Scottsdale

FDA sends warning letters to 41 telehealth platforms selling compounded retatrutide 'titration kits' and fake 'bima' muscle peptides, many filled by Florida pharmacies shielded by a 2035 state statute. FDA says the statute is preempted. An estimated 4.9M Americans now use compounded or telehealth peptides

open_tensions: The muscle-preserving co-pack goes to the people who need it least. It costs $799 cash, Medicare excludes it pending a coverage analysis, and its trial had few over-70s and no fracture data. Meanwhile ≈2.4M Medicare users meet sarcopenia criteria and ≈22,000 excess hip fractures a year are billed to Part A. Whether CMS pays, and at what price above $179, is the 2037 fight.

Public money is now the default payer, but the HRSA program is a capped $8.5B appropriation with ≈600k on waitlists. Small employers are dropping coverage so their workers qualify, which is the crowd-out CBO warned of. Each waitlist month is a forced stop and another cycle.

US generic semaglutide is parked again, behind the first filer's suit against FDA's forfeiture determination. The public rate of $179 is many times the $5–30 Indian price, and the gray market has moved up-market into compounded next-generation molecules through Florida pharmacies whose state shield FDA says is preempted. Safe Pens is still stalled.

About 150,000 children aged 6–11 are now on semaglutide, and about one child in two lives with a medicated parent. The growth data, the adolescent bone-accrual signal (≈-0.2 z-score) and the question of what happens when children stop all arrive after the political fight over the approval, not before it.
still_true: No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is on the US market; generic_us remains false.
Oral starting doses (Wegovy pill, Foundayo) are still $149–150 a month cash through the federal direct-pricing portal (launched as TrumpRx) and manufacturer direct channels.
Congress has passed no importation or authentication law: the 'Safe Pens' bill is still stalled, and FDA still does not prosecute individual users.
The May 2034 NAION class Warnings and Precautions statement remains on every GLP-1 receptor agonist label, including low-dose subscription products, and is still not boxed.
The FTC consent orders on 'calm' and 'focus' subscription brands stand: no 'anxiety treatment' claims.

prose.headline: Washington Now Pays for Thin. Muscle Costs $799 Extra.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2036 more than one American adult in three is on an incretin drug, and for the first time the government pays for more of those prescriptions than employers do. This did not come from a new philosophy. It came from a midterm election. Through the 2034 campaign, candidates in both parties held up the parked generic and the portal price rise, and in July 2035 the Metabolic Health Access Act passed with both sides claiming it. Medicare and Medicaid now pay $179 a month, down from $199. The Part D copay is $25, or nothing for low-income seniors. Seven more states took the permanent ninety-percent Medicaid match. Community health centres hand out the 50-milligram pill free to uninsured adults and to people whose employers do not cover the drug, out of an eight-and-a-half-billion-dollar appropriation that is already running waitlists. In the same month Novo and Lilly cut portal prices by about fifty to eighty dollars in exchange for three quiet years and a tariff exemption. Prices went down, but they went down through negotiation, and brands still sell at two hundred dollars or more.

The poorest users benefited first. About two million people who had been buying Indian pens by parcel moved onto public product, and use in the bottom income third rose faster than anywhere else. Small employers noticed that their workers now qualified for the free program if the company stopped covering the drug, and some stopped. Benefits consultants call this rationalisation. The Congressional Budget Office calls it crowd-out.

The bodies did not converge. In April 2035 the Medicare Trustees counted the fractures for the first time: about twenty-two thousand extra hip fractures a year, roughly a billion dollars billed to the part of Medicare that does not pay for the drug. The muscle and bone problem now has an official name, a grant programme and a DEXA scan at enrolment. In March 2036 Lilly sold the fix, a co-pack of tirzepatide and a monthly muscle-sparing antibody that holds lean mass to about a tenth of the weight lost. It costs $799 a month. Medicare's rate does not cover it, and its trial included almost no one over seventy. The new shape is called the Forte body: thin, full-shouldered, and paid for in cash. In Scottsdale it is a uniform. Across the city in Maryvale, women of the same age on the free pill weigh the same and their scans say something different.

The gray market did not disappear. It moved up-market. Parcel imports fell, and telehealth sites selling compounded retatrutide and so-called bima peptides grew to nearly five million customers, many supplied by Florida pharmacies under a state law that the FDA calls preempted. In June the agency sent forty-one warning letters. The Safe Pens bill was stripped from the Act and is still in committee. The generic is still parked, this time behind a lawsuit.

In November 2035 the FDA approved semaglutide for children aged six to eleven, and Medicaid's children's benefit covered it automatically. About a hundred and fifty thousand children started in the first year. Paediatricians are divided, and the growth data have not yet arrived.

The grey, the flatness people talked about, became a line in a label. A federally funded randomised trial found it in about one in eleven users at the top retatrutide dose and found nothing measurable at the low 'calm' doses. It also found no calm at those doses. The subscription brands removed the word from their homepages. The trial made the drug ordinary for most users, and that was its main effect.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ortiz's alarm goes off at 5:10 in Maryvale. She takes the pill with four ounces of water and waits thirty minutes, as the leaflet says, folding scrubs while she waits. The bottle carries the clinic's label: Community Metabolic Health Program, $0.00.

Her granddaughter Ari, who is nine, is asleep on the couch. Thursday is shot night. Ari's mother does it, holding the pen against Ari's thigh while Ari counts to ten in Spanish. The growth chart from the pediatric clinic is on the fridge under a Suns magnet, with a dot every three months.

At seven Denise drives to Mrs. Kessler's house in Scottsdale. Mrs. Kessler is seventy-four, nine weeks out from a hip pinning, and still on Medicare semaglutide during a bone pause the surgeon argued for. Denise helps her into the shower chair. Mrs. Kessler's daughter comes by with iced coffee. She has the new shoulders, and she says the muscle shot cramps her calves but is worth every penny.

At lunch Denise eats a protein cup in the car and scrolls the clinic portal. Her six-month weigh-in is due Friday at the kiosk by the pharmacy. One miss is allowed. She has already used it, in March, when her car died.

At dinner her son-in-law Marco shows her a box that came in the mail: retatrutide, compounded, from a website with a Tampa return address. He says the clinic waitlist is eleven weeks.

Denise reads the lot number aloud while he checks it against the list on his phone.

rationale.badness: Measured against 2026, this world carries the full 2034 inheritance.
